title: Microeconomics Adventure 2: Elasticities (PED, PES, YED, XED)
welcome_lead: Today you'll stretch your understanding of price, income and cross elasticity.
meta_desc: Economics: price elasticity of demand and supply, income and cross elasticity.
final_note: You computed and interpreted four elasticity measures.

walkthroughs.body_html:
PED = %ΔQd ÷ %ΔP.

|PED| > 1: elastic — total revenue moves opposite to price.
|PED| < 1: inelastic — total revenue moves with price.
|PED| = 1: unit elastic — revenue constant.

Determinants: number of substitutes, share of income, necessity vs luxury, time.

PES = %ΔQs ÷ %ΔP.

Inelastic in the short run (factory capacity fixed), more elastic in the long run.

Determinants: spare capacity, stocks, factor mobility, time, ease of entry.

YED = %ΔQd ÷ %ΔY. Positive = normal good; negative = inferior; > 1 = luxury.

XED = %ΔQd of A ÷ %ΔP of B.
+ve: substitutes (tea vs coffee).
−ve: complements (cars vs petrol).
≈ 0: unrelated.
